P01-009.device_notes: 17-verse unit, one verse past the 14-16 stretch cap; disclosed rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut, as at oshb:Ezek.4.1-4.17, since no refrain-plus-fresh-onset pair stands anywhere inside 5:1-5:17 to license a shorter cut. Paseq at 5:1 and 5:7 disclosed count-only, single-witness. Marks after 5:4 (pe), 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 (samekh) and 5:10 (pe) are disclosed as intra-row, single-witness texture. Three of those five marks do coincide with a formula onset on the verse following them. The pe after 5:4 stands before the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.5.5, and the samekh marks after 5:6 and 5:7 stand before the messenger formulae at oshb:Ezek.5.7 and oshb:Ezek.5.8; each of those three verses belongs to the 122-verse messenger-formula class and each carries the formula verse-initially, 5:7 behind לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Ezek.5.7) and 5:8 behind לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Ezek.5.8). The remaining two do not: oshb:Ezek.5.10 opens on לָכֵ֗ן with no messenger formula, and oshb:Ezek.5.11 opens on the oath with the utterance signature attached mid-verse. No one of the five is read as a unit-cutting seam, and the reason is not any absence of coincidence: a messenger formula opens a sub-onset only where the addressee changes or where the verse before it ends on a close-role formula, and not one of these marks follows a verse that ENDS on such a formula, since none of 5:4, 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 or 5:10 is counted among the utterance-formula verses or in the 64-member recognition family; a parashah mark by itself cannot license the cut. Single witness: a pe stands after MT 4:17, the mark on record at the seam where this unit begins.
P01-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 5:13 or 5:15, the first two 'I Yahweh have spoken' occurrences, to shorten the unit. Rejected because neither is followed by a fresh onset device - the material after each continues the same verdict speech without a messenger formula, word-event or address restarting it - so only 5:17's occurrence is unit-final. The stronger rival, weighed here, is the 5:4/5:5 seam, a division of the chapter that sets the sign-act 5:1-4 against the interpretation 5:5-17. Its far face carries a PE recorded after oshb:Ezek.5.4 and nothing further: that verse ends מִמֶּ֥נּוּ תֵצֵא אֵ֖שׁ אֶל כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and it is counted neither among the utterance-formula verses nor in the 64-member recognition family, so it does not close on a close-role formula. Its near face is genuinely strong, oshb:Ezek.5.5 carrying the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה verse-initially, “The Lord Yahweh says” (web:Ezek.5.5). But a messenger formula is a sub-onset only where the addressee changes or the preceding verse has closed on a verse-final close-role formula, and neither condition holds at this seam: 5:4 addresses the prophet in the 2ms while 5:5 carries no second person at all, the shift to 2mp arriving only at 5:7 and to 2fs at 5:8; and a parashah mark cannot meet the second condition by itself. The row accordingly holds the seam on those stated grounds, and the PE is recorded as corroboration of the rival and not of this unit's onset.

P01-013.boundary_rationale: Onset: 7:5 reopens with a fresh messenger formula immediately after 7:4's pe-marked recognition close — כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.7.5) “The Lord Yahweh says: 'A disaster! A unique disaster! Behold, it comes.” (web:Ezek.7.5). Close: 7:9, the 2mp recognition-family close carrying an appended participle, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.7.9) “Then you will know that I, Yahweh, strike.” (web:Ezek.7.9); this recognition member also carries the doubled “My eye will not spare” (web:Ezek.7.4) refrain — MEASURED at 5 verses book-wide (5:11, 7:4, 7:9, 8:18, 9:10) by a consonantal-skeleton sweep of the phrase *lo tachos eini* over the pointed Hebrew witness, the WEB contracting the clause at every one of those verses except 7:4, which is why the English quoted here is taken from web:Ezek.7.4 — the same refrain the close at 7:4 already carries, so 7:9 closes a distinct short unit before the unmarked doom-poem reopens at 7:10 with no formula of its own.

P02-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.10.1 וָאֶרְאֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֶל הָרָקִ֨יעַ֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל רֹ֣אשׁ הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים כְּאֶ֣בֶן סַפִּ֔יר כְּמַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כִּסֵּ֑א נִרְאָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם opens the throne-like sapphire vision with no transport verb and no formula at all — the scene continues directly from 9:11 with a bare 'then I looked, and behold'. The row is anchored instead on the glory's own movement: oshb:Ezek.10.4 וַיָּ֤רָם כְּבוֹד יְהוָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל הַכְּר֔וּב עַ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן הַבָּ֑יִת וַיִּמָּלֵ֤א הַבַּ֨יִת֙ אֶת הֶ֣עָנָ֔ן וְהֶֽחָצֵר֙ מָֽלְאָ֔ה אֶת נֹ֖גַהּ כְּב֥וֹד יְהוָֽה records כבוד יהוה rising from the cherub to the house's threshold (sweep: 9 verses book-wide carry כבוד יהוה — 1:28, 3:12, 3:23, 10:4, 10:18, 11:23, 43:4, 43:5, 44:4, the departure/return arc), the first stage of the glory's exit. Close: oshb:Ezek.10.8 וַיֵּרָ֖א לַכְּרֻבִ֑ים תַּבְנִית֙ יַד אָדָ֔ם תַּ֖חַת כַּנְפֵיהֶֽם — the hand of a man under the cherubim's wings — closes the coal-taking errand before the row turns to the extended wheel description. Both sides: a samekh follows oshb:Ezek.9.11 immediately before this row's onset (single-witness), giving Masoretic corroboration to the seam behind it, even though the onset verse oshb:Ezek.10.1 itself carries no mark; the close carries no parashah mark either (chapter 10 carries none at all, disclosed below), so the close-side seam rests on content alone — the coal-fire task is complete and the following verses shift from narrated action to sustained physical description.
P02-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating all of 10:1-17 (the errand plus the wheel description) as one row was weighed, since nothing but content separates them. It was not taken because 10:9-17 is a self-contained descriptive unit in its own right and folding it in here would produce a seventeen-verse row (MEASURED: web:Ezek.10.1-Ezek.10.17 runs to 17 verses, counted on its WEB face) with no internal anchor of any kind in an already mark-free chapter.

P02-009.device_notes: Filed as salvation_oracle per the restoration promise that is the unit's burden (gather-and-return is stated here: MEASURED at oshb:Ezek.11.17 the oracle both gathers and gives the land — the consonantal skeleton carries וקבצתי אתכם מן העמים ואספתי אתכם מן הארצות and ונתתי לכם את אדמת ישראל, which the WEB renders “I will gather you from the peoples, and assemble you out of the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.” (web:Ezek.11.17) — and the “one heart… heart of flesh” (web:Ezek.11.19) promise stands alongside it, so the salvation_oracle filing rests on the device the unit actually carries); a one-sentence deviation is disclosed because the unit also carries a disputation-oracle color (the quoted Jerusalem claim at 11:15 is refuted before the promise is given), and the category is not read as free text beyond that single disclosure. No K/Q or paseq falls in this span.
P02-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Holding 11:14-21 inside a single long 11:1-21 courtyard-and-oracle row, with the word-event at 11:14 disclosed only as internal texture, was weighed as an alternative reading. It was not taken because 11:14 is a strict word-event onset (not a bare transition) and the oracle's own addressee — the scattered exiles — differs from the courtyard men addressed in 11:1-13, which is enough of a class shift to justify treating it as its own formula-bounded row even while the wider vision frame stays open around it. A second rival sits inside this row and is weighed here: a seam at 11:16/11:17. In this witness a samekh sits on MT 11:15 and another on MT 11:16, and because each mark is keyed to the verse it stands after, both fall immediately before a verse that carries the long messenger formula כה אמר אדני יהוה — oshb:Ezek.11.16 and oshb:Ezek.11.17, two of that class's 122 verses. Neither seam is a licensed messenger sub-onset, which would need a change of addressee or a verse before it ending on a close-role formula. The addressee holds steady: the son-of-man address and the scattered exiles are named at 11:15 and nothing readdresses the oracle before 11:21. Nor does either preceding verse finish on a close-role formula — MEASURED on the pointed witness, MT 11:15 finishes לָ֥נוּ הִ֛יא נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה (oshb:Ezek.11.15) and MT 11:16 finishes בָּאֲרָצ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.11.16), while in 11:16 and in 11:17 alike the messenger formula stands at the verse's head after לכן אמר rather than at its end. No mark can stand in for that verse-final close by itself, so the two samekhs are disclosed for the paragraph structure they corroborate within the row, and the row rests on its strict word-event onset at 11:14 and its verse-final utterance close at 11:21 (MEASURED: נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה closes MT 11:21) (oshb:Ezek.11.15, oshb:Ezek.11.21).

P02-017.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.13.10 יַ֣עַן וּבְיַ֜עַן הִטְע֧וּ אֶת עַמִּ֛י לֵאמֹ֥ר שָׁל֖וֹם וְאֵ֣ין שָׁל֑וֹם וְהוּא֙ בֹּ֣נֶה חַ֔יִץ וְהִנָּ֛ם טָחִ֥ים אֹת֖וֹ תָּפֵֽל turns to the whitewash-wall metaphor “Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying,” 'Peace', “and there is no peace.” (web:Ezek.13.10), with a fresh messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.13.13. Close: oshb:Ezek.13.16 נְבִיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַֽנִבְּאִים֙ אֶל יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְהַחֹזִ֥ים לָ֖הּ חֲז֣וֹן שָׁלֹ֑ם וְאֵ֣ין שָׁלֹ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה, naming “the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem… visions of peace… and there is no peace” (web:Ezek.13.16); a pe follows this verse (single-witness), and an OSHB editorial note (single-witness apparatus) also falls here. Both sides: the onset continues the ch.13 indictment without an addressee change (so it is a sub-onset, not a fresh row-grade onset on its own merits) but the messenger-formula-plus-utterance-close bracket at the far end is clean and pe-corroborated.

P02-019.strongest_rejected_alternative: Opening the row at 14:2, the word-event proper, rather than at 14:1 is the rival that matters, and it is weighed below. Its near face is strong: oshb:Ezek.14.2 carries the strict word-event formula, one of that class's 39 verses. Its far face is the elders' scene at oshb:Ezek.14.1, which carries no formula of its own. The parashah layer speaks for the RIVAL and not for this row, and it is written up that way: MEASURED in this witness's paragraph marks, a pe stands on MT 14:1, and that layer keys a break to the verse it follows, so the witness parts 14:1 from 14:2 — exactly where the rival would cut. Since no mark licenses a seam on its own, the corroboration is disclosed and left unadopted. The row opens at 14:1 all the same, on two stated grounds. First, this chapter divides with the elders' scene at the head of the unit: 14:1 comes before the word-event at 14:2, and the row opens at 14:1. Second, the bar on a row under three verses that is not a complete word-event unit forbids the one-verse row at 14:1 that the rival's cut would leave behind, 14:1 being no complete word-event unit. Holding against a licensed two-faced rival on stated grounds is what grades this row medium.

P02-020.device_notes: MT 14:14 and MT 14:20 both carry the Qere-adaptation editorial note class disclosed above, in addition to the ordinary ketiv/qere note at each verse (ketiv דנאל, qere דָּנִיֵּ֣אל (oshb:Ezek.14.14 and oshb:Ezek.14.20) — the shorter legendary-figure spelling against the fuller ‘Daniel’ reading); both disclosures are given at both verses since they are two independent single-witness apparatus facts about the same word. Paseq at 14:21 is count-only. oshb:Ezek.15.1 is cited above only as forward-side onset evidence for the seam; it is not a row here. Length: this row is 12 verses (MEASURED: web:Ezek.14.12-Ezek.14.23, counted on the WEB face), set against a 7-10 verse target. The over-length is disclosed and carried rather than hidden: the four-scourge refrain list is never cut inside itself, and the one internal seam a reader might take, the messenger paragraph at 14:21, is weighed and held in the rejected alternative.
P02-020.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at oshb:Ezek.14.20, where a pe falls after the fourth triad refrain and immediately before the oracle turns from the hypothetical four scourges to their explicit application to Jerusalem (14:21-23), is the standing rival, and it is weighed face by face rather than passed over. MT 14:21 does open on a messenger formula: MEASURED on the witness's consonantal skeleton, oshb:Ezek.14.21 begins כי כה אמר אדני יהוה, and that verse is one of the 122 verses of the long messenger-formula class. What it opens is nonetheless a paragraph, not a sub-onset, since a messenger formula counts as a sub-onset only when the addressee is new or when the verse just before it ENDS on a close-role formula, and neither condition is met. Nothing marks a new addressee at 14:21 — MEASURED, the son-of-man address falls at MT 14:3 and MT 14:13 and at no other verse of this chapter, chapter 14 carries no set-your-face verse at all, and 14:21 is not opened by 'and you, son of man' — so what turns there is the subject, from a hypothetical land to Jerusalem, and not the person addressed. As for the other condition, the utterance formula in MT 14:20 does NOT reach the verse end: MEASURED, נאם אדני יהוה sits at characters 29 through 41 of an 81-character skeleton, the first character counted as 1 and both ends included, and the independent clause אם בן אם בת יצילו המה בצדקתם יצילו נפשם runs from there to the sof pasuq. So the pe on MT 14:20 is entered as support for the rival it favours and for no more than that: this witness records a break against the verse before it, a mark cannot supply a verse-final close, and paragraph evidence informs while every licensed driver outranks it. The row carries on to its own verse-final utterance close at oshb:Ezek.14.23.

P05-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 23:22 opens with the messenger formula directly addressing Oholibah by name (addressee shift from third-person dual narrative to second-person singular verdict), whole verse = "לָכֵ֣ן אָהֳלִיבָ֗ה כֹּֽה אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנְנִ֨י מֵעִ֤יר אֶת מְאַהֲבַ֨יִךְ֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר נָקְעָ֥ה נַפְשֵׁ֖ךְ מֵהֶ֑ם וַהֲבֵאתִ֥ים עָלַ֖יִךְ מִסָּבִֽיב (oshb:Ezek.23.22)", corroborated behind by the samekh at 23:21 (the close of the prior unit). Close: 23:35, whole verse = "לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֚עַן שָׁכַ֣חַתְּ אוֹתִ֔י וַתַּשְׁלִ֥יכִי אוֹתִ֖י אַחֲרֵ֣י גַוֵּ֑ךְ וְגַם אַ֛תְּ שְׂאִ֥י זִמָּתֵ֖ךְ וְאֶת תַּזְנוּתָֽיִךְ (oshb:Ezek.23.35)" — a "therefore... because" verdict-summary still addressed to the same singular addressee, immediately before 23:36 shifts to a dual/plural addressee (both sisters together, weighed as the following unit's onset). CLOSE-SEAM MARK: MEASURED in the pointed witness, MT 23:35 is followed by a SAMEKH (setumah, closed section, single-witness). Because a mark is recorded on the verse it follows, this one stands on THIS row's close seam at 23:35/23:36 - not behind the onset and not mid-unit - so the close is corroborated on its near face by the mark and on its far face by the addressee-count shift at 23:36. A licensed text signal outranks a section mark, so the samekh is weak corroboration and decides nothing alone. One further measured fact is stated here without being acted on, because it bears on the rejected alternative rather than on this disclosure: MT 23:34 ends verse-finally on the utterance formula (oshb:Ezek.23.34), which means the messenger formula opening MT 23:35 stands right after a verse that ends on a close-role formula, and that alone licenses it as a sub-onset, so the 23:34/23:35 rival is a licensed, two-faced rival and not one defeated by addressee continuity alone. The close stays at 23:35 and the row stands at medium, the grade a seam earns when it is kept on stated grounds against a licensed rival with evidence on both faces; the question of that seam remains open.

P05-007.strongest_rejected_alternative: Two alternatives were weighed for MT 24:1. (1) Treating 24:1-27 as ONE unit (24:1 as the head of this collection's entire last movement, no further internal cut) — rejected because 24:15 carries its own full-form strict word-event onset (a hard seam in its own right) and a genre shift from mashal to sign-act, and both halves carry independent formula closes (24:14 and 24:27); collapsing them would also violate the granularity target. (2) Treating 24:1 as its OWN one-verse dated complex, separate from 24:2-14 — rejected because a dateline fused with a word-event in one verse is treated as a single onset that never splits, and because 24:3's dateline-day reference (verse-final words "שְׁפֹ֔ת וְגַם יְצֹ֥ק בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם (oshb:Ezek.24.3)") ties the mashal directly to the date just given, with no seam between them. (3) Cutting at 24:8/24:9 - the alternative the Masoretic paragraph layer proposes, named and weighed here with its mark as corroboration. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 24:9 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.24.9). What its far face carries: MEASURED in the witness's paragraph marks, MT 24:8 is followed by a PE (petuchah, open section, single-witness) - and nothing else, because MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness MT 24:8 ends on a purpose infinitive (oshb:Ezek.24.8), with no utterance, recognition or I-YHWH-have-spoken signature anywhere in that verse. Whether a messenger sub-onset is licensed there: it is NOT. The addressee condition fails, because the addressee does not change - MT 24:6 already addresses the bloody city (oshb:Ezek.24.6) and MT 24:9 addresses that same city. The close condition fails too, because the verse immediately before it does not END on a close-role formula, and a mark alone never stands in for that close. The stated ground on which this row holds: a section mark gives way to a licensed text signal, so the PE after MT 24:8 is weak corroboration and is disclosed FOR the alternative it corroborates, not for this row, and it is outranked by the licensed drivers this row does rest on - the fused dateline-plus-word-event onset at 24:1 and the stacked I-YHWH-have-spoken plus utterance close at 24:14. So the 24:8/24:9 cut is a mark-only, paragraph-grade rival: weighed, disclosed and held, and a rival of that kind is never fatal to this row's grade.
P05-007.device_notes: Dateline 24:1 counted among the book's 14 oracle datelines and in the 41-verse word-event any-form count; ABSENT from the strict 39-verse count because the year-month-day clause infixes between the two adjacency-anchor words the strict pattern requires; the 39/41/48/49-verse word-event counts are never blended. A single ketiv/qere pair sits at 24:2, its Qere reserved to the note layer rather than quoted here. Paseq at 24:6 (count-only, single-witness, unsourceable intra-verse position).

P05-008.device_notes: Paseq at 24:17 and 24:21 (count-only, single-witness, unsourceable intra-verse position). 24:24's recognition-pattern clause (2mp, Lord-YHWH variant, a member of the counted adonai-form class) is disclosed as mid-unit, paragraph-final rather than unit-final, since a refrain closes the unit it stands in, not necessarily the whole span, when the material after it is that same unit's own payoff (24:25-27). Samekh at 24:27 (single-witness) is both this unit's close and the parent collection's own close. Marks are disclosed in all three directions. MEASURED in this witness, MT 24:14 is followed by a PE (petuchah, OPEN section, single-witness), recorded on the verse it follows, so it stands behind this row's ONSET seam at 24:14/24:15. The interior direction carries a single-witness samekh after MT 24:24 (disclosed here) and the close direction the samekh after MT 24:27 (disclosed above), completing the three directions. A licensed text signal outranks a section mark, so the PE is weak corroboration; this onset rests on the full-form strict word-event formula at 24:15.

P06-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:1 opens "וַיְהִ֛י בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1) — an explicit month+day dateline (“In the eleventh year, in the first of the month”, web:Ezek.26.1, WEB) together with the PERFECT-form word-event, "הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1), the 7-verse hayah family the dated oracles use after their dateline, a HARD seam and the strongest onset class in the book. In the WEB, “In the eleventh year, in the first of the month, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.26.1). 26:2 supplies the accusation, "בֶּן אָדָ֗ם יַ֠עַן אֲשֶׁר אָ֨מְרָה צֹּ֤ר עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הֶאָ֔ח נִשְׁבְּרָ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעַמִּ֖ים נָסֵ֣בָּה אֵלָ֑י אִמָּלְאָ֖ה הָחֳרָֽבָה" (oshb:Ezek.26.2), quoting Tyre's own "Aha!" against Jerusalem. Close (both sides): 26:6 ends "וּבְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה בַּחֶ֖רֶב תֵּהָרַ֑גְנָה וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.6), the strict 3mp recognition formula, with a PE immediately after. Ahead, 26:7 reopens with a fresh messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל צֹ֗ר…", oshb:Ezek.26.7) introducing Nebuchadnezzar's siege — a new speech unit against the same addressee, not an addressee change, which is why it is held as its own row rather than folded in here: the refrain at 26:6 closes THIS unit.

P06-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:11 opens with the strict word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.28.11). 28:12 supplies the genre command, "בֶּן אָדָ֕ם שָׂ֥א קִינָ֖ה עַל מֶ֣לֶךְ צ֑וֹר וְאָמַ֣רְתָּ לּ֗וֹ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אַתָּה֙ חוֹתֵ֣ם תָּכְנִ֔ית מָלֵ֥א חָכְמָ֖ה וּכְלִ֥יל יֹֽפִי" — “Son of man, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre” (web:Ezek.28.12, WEB) — the same imperative-plus-קִינָ֖ה anchor as 27:2, naming the addressee "king" (מֶ֣לֶךְ (oshb:Ezek.28.12)) rather than 28:2's "prince" (לִנְגִ֨יד (oshb:Ezek.28.2)). In the WEB, “Son of man, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre, and tell him, ‘The Lord Yahweh says:” (web:Ezek.28.12). Close (both sides): 28:19 ends "כָּל יוֹדְעֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּֽעַמִּ֔ים שָׁמְמ֖וּ עָלֶ֑יךָ בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔יתָ וְאֵינְךָ֖ עַד עוֹלָֽם" (oshb:Ezek.28.19) with a PE immediately after and no recognition/utterance/"I YHWH have spoken" formula present; the close pattern “You have become a terror, and you will exist no more.” (web:Ezek.28.19, WEB) mirrors MT 27:36's terminal clause in the CONSONANTAL Hebrew and not in the translation - MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, the two verses end consonant for consonant on the same four words and differ only in the Masoretic pointing, feminine singular at MT 27:36 against masculine singular at MT 28:19, while the WEB renders MT 27:36 quite differently as “You have come to a terrible end, and you will be no more.” (web:Ezek.27.36, WEB); the exact mirror holds of the Hebrew consonants alone. Behind, 28:10 closed the prince-of-Tyre unit on the stacked "I have spoken" + utterance close and a SAMEKH; ahead, 28:20 opens a fresh strict word-event onset for the Sidon oracle.

P07-001.strongest_rejected_alternative: Three alternatives are weighed. (1) Ending the row at 29:6, where an extended (non-strict) recognition-type close occurs; rejected because 29:7 continues the same staff-of-reed image with no intervening onset, and because this chapter's own onset/close collision pattern places the true seam after 29:9, not 29:6. Two further readings are weighed. (2) Cutting at 29:7/29:8 - the alternative the paragraph layer proposes, where the witness's division is disclosed as corroboration for that alternative: MEASURED in this witness's section marks, MT 29:7 is followed by a SAMEKH (setumah, closed section, single-witness), recorded on the verse it follows, and MT 29:7 additionally carries one ketiv/qere pair, already disclosed in this row. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 29:8 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.29.8), and with it a grammatical addressee shift - MT 29:7 addresses a masculine singular and MT 29:8 a feminine singular (oshb:Ezek.29.7, oshb:Ezek.29.8), that is, from Pharaoh to the land. Whether a messenger sub-onset is licensed there: it IS, since a change of addressee is enough to license one, so this rival is licensed and two-faced and is not dismissed. Its far face is nevertheless thin: MT 29:7 ends with no close-role formula, so the other licensing condition, a verse-final close before the formula, would fail there and only the SAMEKH stands. The stated ground on which this row holds: the crocodile verdict's own refrain is the recognition formula at MT 29:9, and MT 29:10 restates the same charge as a fresh against-you cycle (oshb:Ezek.29.10); a licensed text signal ranks above any section mark, so the SAMEKH after MT 29:7 is weak corroboration and is disclosed FOR this rival, not for this row. When a licensed rival with two faces is held off on grounds stated in the row, the row is graded MEDIUM, and that is this row's grade. (3) Tiling MT 29:1-29:16 as ONE row - a proposed reading of this chapter (EXTRACTED) that runs 29:1-16 with the mid-verse WEB paragraph at 29:9 and the forty-years turn at 29:13 inside it. What supports it: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, no dateline and no word-event formula stands anywhere between MT 29:1 and the next dateline at MT 29:17; MEASURED in the witness's paragraph marks, the only marks inside that stretch follow MT 29:7 and MT 29:12, and NO mark stands on MT 29:9. And this row's own close is the weak shape, a close formula followed inside its verse by an independent clause: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, the recognition formula in MT 29:9 ends at the etnachta and an INDEPENDENT causal clause with a finite verb fills the rest of the verse (oshb:Ezek.29.9) - unlike MT 29:6, whose words after its own recognition clause are a causal phrase built on an infinitive construct (oshb:Ezek.29.6), a dependent completion that grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal rather than the weak mid-verse shape. The stated ground on which this row holds: MT 29:10 opens a fresh against-you verdict cycle restating the charge, so the collision is resolved at the verse boundary after 29:9. The weakness of the 29:9 close and the proposed 29:1-16 reading are disclosed rather than argued away; they are why this row is graded medium and not high.

P08-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: a fresh messenger formula at Ezek.36.13 כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֚עַן אֹמְרִ֣ים לָכֶ֔ם אֹכֶ֥לֶת אָדָ֖ם אתי וּמְשַׁכֶּ֥לֶת גויך הָיִֽית (oshb:Ezek.36.13) opens immediately after the refrain-grade close and samekh mark at oshb:Ezek.36.12, itself licensed as a cutting seam by the addressee change from the 2mp/2ms address of Ezek.36.1-Ezek.36.12 (‘you,’ the mountains) to the 2fs address (‘you,’ feminine singular, the land) that opens here — satisfying the seam condition from this side as well as from the close side. MT 36.13 and MT 36.14 are BOTH doubled-note K/Q verses (two Qere each): oshb:Ezek.36.13 carries ketiv 'אתי' / qere 'אָ֑תְּ' (‘you,’ feminine singular) and, as the unpointed last word of וּמְשַׁכֶּ֥לֶת גויך, a second ketiv read as qere 'גּוֹיַ֖יִךְ' ('your nation' plene); oshb:Ezek.36.14 carries ketiv 'וגויך' / qere 'וְגוֹיַ֖יִךְ' and ketiv 'תכשלי' / qere 'תְשַׁכְּלִי'. Of those four notes, morpheme separators are present in the K/Q layer -- and therefore stripped in the forms as rendered here -- only for the SECOND 36:13 note (2 separators) and the FIRST 36:14 note (4); the first 36:13 note and the second 36:14 note carry none in the layer at all, so nothing was stripped from either of them. MEASURED by counting the '/' morpheme separators in each of the two K/Q notes this witness carries at each of these verses: 36:13 measures [0, 2] and 36:14 measures [4, 0]. Ezek.36.14 also carries the utterance formula, and it recurs at Ezek.36.15 וְלֹא אַשְׁמִ֨יעַ אֵלַ֤יִךְ עוֹד֙ כְּלִמַּ֣ת הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְחֶרְפַּ֥ת עַמִּ֖ים לֹ֣א תִשְׂאִי ע֑וֹד וגויך לֹא תַכְשִׁ֣לִי ע֔וֹד נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.36.15) (itself carrying one more K/Q pair on 'your nation') — a doubled internal utterance close. Close: a samekh mark follows Ezek.36.15, ending this sub-unit before the fresh, formally distinct word-event of Ezek.36.16.

P08-013.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 36.16-32 as one row rather than splitting at 36.23/36.24. Rejected for the same reason as the Ezek.36.16-Ezek.36.23 seam: at 36.23 the knowing clause and the utterance signature together fill the second half of that verse, the formula words sitting inside it rather than at its end, and what follows them as far as the final word is a dependent temporal infinitive and not an independent clause (oshb:Ezek.36.23) -- so the formula is verse-final in effect, a licensed close of the ordinary kind rather than the weak mid-verse case, and 36.24 opens a fresh movement; the split keeps this row inside the 7-10 typical band (9 verses).

P10-005.boundary_rationale: Onset side: this seam carries no formula evidence of its own. 40:38 opens וְלִשְׁכָּ֣ה וּפִתְחָ֔הּ בְּאֵילִ֖ים הַשְּׁעָרִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.40.38), “A room with its door was by the posts at the gates” (web:Ezek.40.38), with a bare vav, no transport verb and no measuring verb -- the topic shifts from gate architecture to the functional furniture used for slaughtering and washing the sacrifices, but nothing in the bytes marks the shift as a formula onset; it rests on content alone, following directly on the north inner gate's close at 40:37. The row continues through the singers' and priests' chambers (40:44-46, including the Zadokite priestly qualification, case-law texture inside a measurement row, disclosed) and closes at 40:47's וְהַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לִפְנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Ezek.40.47) “The altar was before the house” (web:Ezek.40.47), a summary notice before 40:48's transport verb moves the tour into the temple building itself. Both sides of this row are held to a lower confidence than its neighbors precisely because neither its onset nor its close carries a tier-1 device.

P10-006.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:48's transport verb opens וַיְבִאֵנִי֮ אֶל אֻלָ֣ם הַבַּיִת֒ (oshb:Ezek.40.48) “he brought me to the porch of the house” (web:Ezek.40.48), marking entry into the temple building proper, distinct from every court and gate measured before it. A second transport verb follows at 41:1, וַיְבִיאֵ֖נִי אֶל הַהֵיכָ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.41.1) “He brought me to the nave and measured” (web:Ezek.41.1), disclosed here as continuous forward motion through one threshold sequence rather than a fresh row seam, since no formula or refrain close intervenes between the porch and the nave. The two-verse porch description (40:48-49) is held with the four-verse nave description (41:1-4) as one row rather than left as an under-three-verse fragment. Close side: 41:4 ends with וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֖ה קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים (oshb:Ezek.41.4) “He said to me,” then “This is the most holy place.” (web:Ezek.41.4), a genuine speak-formula close, before 41:5's fresh measuring verb turns to a new object, the house wall. This close carries a named speech formula rather than resting on content alone, unlike its neighbors on either side.

P10-008.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 41:12 turns to a different structure from the side-chamber circuit just closed, a change of measured object rather than a bare topic shift: וְהַבִּנְיָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֶל פְּנֵ֨י הַגִּזְרָ֜ה פְּאַ֣ת דֶּֽרֶךְ הַיָּ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.41.12) “The building that was before the separate place at the side toward the west” (web:Ezek.41.12), confirmed by the fresh measuring verb וּמָדַ֣ד אֶת הַבַּ֔יִת (oshb:Ezek.41.13) that opens this row's own accounting of the building. The row carries the temple/separate-place/building triad each measured at a hundred cubits (41:13-14), the rear building and its galleries with a K/Q lexical variant on 'galleries' at oshb:Ezek.41.15 (ואתוקיהא, checked: a form variant, not a numeral), the side-chamber gallery structure (41:16-19), the cherubim-and-palm-tree decorative program running to above the entrance (41:18-20), the doorposts of the nave (41:21), the wooden altar-table with its own speak-formula notice, וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֚ה הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.41.22), its speech rendered “This is the table that is before Yahweh” (web:Ezek.41.22), opened by the 'spoke to me' root, distinct from the 'said to me' form at 41:4, the double doors of the nave and sanctuary (41:23-25), and the repeated cherubim-and-palm-tree pattern closing on the porch threshold. Close side: 41:26 ends וְצַלְע֥וֹת הַבַּ֖יִת וְהָעֻבִּֽים (oshb:Ezek.41.26), “the side rooms of the temple and the thresholds” (web:Ezek.41.26), and the next verse, oshb:Ezek.42.1, moves the tour out to the outer court with its double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי … וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי -- a strong close by contrast, since the following onset is tier-1 even though this row's own onset rests on the measured-object change rather than a formula. The puncta extraordinaria at 41:20, וְקִ֖יר הַׄהֵׄיׄכָֽׄלׄ (oshb:Ezek.41.20), five instances of the upper dot U+05C4, are disclosed single-witness as intra-row texture on the decorative program's own close, not as boundary evidence.

P10-012.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:1's transport verb opens וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל הַשָּׁ֑עַר (oshb:Ezek.43.1) 'he led me to the gate', beginning the named hard seam behind the closed measuring circuit, and the row immediately carries the glory-of-YHWH device twice (43:4, 43:5), part of the book's nine-verse departure/return arc for that idiom, alongside the river-Chebar inclusio at 43:3 (one of eight such verses tying this scene back to Ezek 1 and 10) “and I fell on my face” (web:Ezek.43.3) (one of five verses in which the WEB reads “I fell on my face”). The row turns from vision report to direct address at 43:6-9: a voice from the house, the man beside the prophet, the 'son of man' charge naming YHWH's throne and footstool, and the polemic against the house of Israel's defilement of the sanctuary by royal corpses and high places. Close side: 43:9 ends the divine resolution וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.43.9) “Then I will dwell among them forever” (web:Ezek.43.9) immediately before the samekh (oshb:Ezek.43.9, single-witness) -- the first Masoretic paragraph mark since the pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29, ending a 103-verse unmarked stretch. This is the only row here whose close carries genuine parashah corroboration, and it is disclosed as single-witness even so.

P10-013.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:10 opens אַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.43.10) 'you, son of man' directly after the samekh (single-witness) closing at oshb:Ezek.43.9 -- a near-form of the book's twenty-three-verse 'and you, son of man' sub-onset family, here without the leading vav, disclosed as such rather than counted against that sweep. It charges the prophet to show the house's pattern so Israel may be ashamed of its iniquities. Close side: 43:12 closes on a doubled envelope formula, זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת ... הִנֵּה זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֥ת הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Ezek.43.12) “This is the law of the house” (web:Ezek.43.12) ... “Behold, this is the law of the house” (web:Ezek.43.12), repeating the title at the top and bottom of the same verse -- a strong lexical close-device, and the reason this three-verse span is held as its own row despite its length: the inclusio is a self-contained frame around 43:10-12 that a larger row would have to break through rather than around.

P10-014.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:13 opens with an explicit topic header, וְאֵ֨לֶּה מִדּ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ (oshb:Ezek.43.13), the vav-initial “These are the measurements of the altar” (web:Ezek.43.13), functioning as a list-onset in the same way such headers do elsewhere in the book, immediately after the doubled inclusio that closes 43:12. The row descends through the altar's base, lower and greater ledges, hearth and horns, in cubit-and-handbreadth units, one of which (43:15) carries two OSHB editors' notes, one marking an anomalous form and one recording a ketiv/qere decision the editors take with the Leningrad Codex against BHS, while the span's one K/Q note stands at 43:16. Close side: 43:17 ends with the steps 'toward the east' before 43:18 opens with the messenger formula, a clean tier-1 onset on the far side even though this row's own close rests on content completion rather than a refrain.

P11-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: the messenger formula at Ezek.47.13 (thus says the Lord GOD, then “This shall be the border” (web:Ezek.47.13)) opens the land-division topic, a genre shift from the river vision behind it -- the hard seam at 47.12/47.13. The row covers the overall border statement and Joseph's double portion (13-14), the border's four sides in sequence, north/east/south/west (15-20), and the instruction to divide the land by lot including resident aliens (21-23). Close: the samekh recorded after Ezek.47.23 co-occurs with the utterance signature in the same verse -- a doubled close signal (formula close plus parashah mark on the same verse), recurring at 48.29.

P11-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: a transport verb at Ezek.47.1 (“He brought me back to the door of the temple” (web:Ezek.47.1)) continues the vision after the hard seam at 46.24/47.1; a second transport verb follows immediately at 47.2, then the measuring sequence proper (3-5, four successive measured wadings) -- disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation from a pure vision_report, since the passage briefly carries temple_measurement's own device before returning to vision narrative. The row covers the river's rise from the threshold (1-2), the four measured wadings (3-5), the 'have you seen, son of man' address (6) and the return to the bank, the riverside trees and the healed sea (7-10), the unhealed swamps (11, a K/Q verse), and the closing description of the riverbank trees bearing monthly fruit (12), where the construction glossed 'its months' is disclosed as the book's final chodesh-root homograph, not a date formula. Close: the samekh recorded after Ezek.47.12 ends the row; the next verse, 47.13, opens with a fresh messenger formula addressed to the land-division topic -- a genre shift from vision to statute/allotment, the hard seam at 47.12/47.13.
P11-010.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 47.5/47.6 to isolate the measuring circuit (47.3-5) as its own temple_measurement row. Weighed face by face and held on stated grounds. The rival's near face, Ezek.47.6, IS licensed: the verse is both a said-to-me verse and a guided-motion verse (וַיּוֹלִכֵ֥נִי, וַיְשִׁבֵ֖נִי), and it is one of the 20 verses in the closed transport-verb class, so a seam there would not be device-free. Its far face, Ezek.47.5, carries the fourth measure-verb occurrence and a content close (נַ֖חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יֵעָבֵֽר), with no close-role formula and no parashah mark, so the rival is one-faced rather than two-faced. The row holds against it on three stated grounds: Ezek.47.6's question looks BACK at the measuring just reported and its motion returns the prophet to the bank inside one scene rather than opening a new one; 47:1-12 is read as a single region with 47:6 inside it as interior texture; and the only further signal at 47:6 is the WEB's mid-verse paragraph, which is tier-4 and never corroborates a seam. MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, Ezek.47.3 does not BEGIN with a guided-motion verb (it opens בְּצֵאת הָאִ֥ישׁ) but does carry וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי later in the verse, and Ezek.47.4 carries that same form twice. Whether those tokens belong to the transport class that can bound a row is an open question, so no membership claim is made here in either direction. The measuring sequence therefore remains texture inside the single river vision running 47.1-12, disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation rather than split into a separate row (oshb:Ezek.47.5, oshb:Ezek.47.3, oshb:Ezek.47.6).
